### Front line

According to the Ukrainian monitoring group DeepStateMap, territorial changes compared to the previous day showed 2.3 square kilometres newly occupied by Russian forces (shifting from contested), 6.2 square kilometres newly contested, and 0.3 square kilometres returning to Ukrainian control. Contested shifts specifically affected the settlements of Novyi Donbas in Donetsk Oblast (61% of the village area newly contested) and Vozdvyzhivka in Zaporizhzhia Oblast (1% newly contested).

The Russian Ministry of Defence claimed that its "North" grouping was tightening an encirclement around Ukrainian forces in northeastern Kharkiv Oblast, alleging ongoing fighting in the areas of Varvarivka, Mykolaivka, Lobanivka, and Reznykove, alongside operations against encircled units near Rublene, Nefedivka, Kupino, and Chorne. The Russian MoD also claimed offensive operations across the Kramatorsk, Zaporizhzhia, and Dnipropetrovsk directions, as well as Sumy Oblast. None of these Russian encirclement or advance claims were independently verified in the provided reports.

### Strikes and losses

The Russian Ministry of Defence reported that overnight and during the day, Russian air defence forces intercepted and destroyed a total of 839 Ukrainian aircraft-type drones across multiple Russian regions, Crimea, and over the Black and Azov seas (559 overnight and 280 during the day). In Ukraine, the Russian MoD claimed drone strikes against a Nova Poshta logistics centre in Chornomorsk, an Odesa data centre, multiple Ukrainian temporary deployment points, and a total of seven dry cargo ships allegedly carrying military cargo across the Black Sea, Odesa, and the Bug Estuary. The Russian MoD also claimed to have struck the Pivnichnyi (Northern) road bridge over the Dnipro River in Kyiv. Independent geolocation platform GeoConfirmed independently verified damage from a Russian strike on the Pivnichnyi Bridge in Kyiv, noting visible cratering.

GeoConfirmed also verified battlefield incidents, including Russian FPV drone strikes against a Ukrainian uncrewed ground vehicle (UGV) and Russian strikes on logistics trucks, as well as a Ukrainian FPV strike on a Russian soldier, the capture of two Russian soldiers, and an explosion following a Ukrainian drone strike on a Russian Ural-based vehicle. WarSpotting independently logged two unknown Russian fighter aircraft destroyed near Khanskaya airbase in Russia.

*The Economist* war-fire model detected 42 war-related satellite fire detections, primarily concentrated in Kherson Oblast (22) and Donetsk Oblast (6).

### Official statements

Ukrainian Defence Minister Yevhenii Khmara claimed that Ukrainian long-range deep strikes have disabled over 51% of Russia's oil refining capacity, citing recent strikes against several facilities including the Moscow, Yaroslavl, KINEF, Ust-Luga, and Perm refineries. In international engagements, Khmara met with German Chancellor Friedrich Merz to request priority air defence equipment—specifically ammunition for F-16s, IRIS-T, and Patriot systems—and signed five documents with German defence firms following a bilateral business forum. 

Conversely, the Russian Ministry of Defence issued a warning that it would intensify strikes against Kyiv and other Ukrainian military and infrastructure targets. Moscow claimed these strikes were direct retaliation for alleged Ukrainian attacks on Russian civilian targets, citing claimed drone attacks on Moscow and an overnight attack on residential quarters in Belgorod. The Russian MoD placed "full personal and political responsibility" for further escalated strikes on Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy.
